heading.text: 3D model generation (only when you use a 3D model skill)

description.text: This provider is only used when you invoke a 3D model generation skill. If you never use the 3D models app, none of your data is shared with it.

Hi3D receives reference images you supply or images generated from your text prompt, plus generation settings. Its Terms license Inputs and Outputs for AI model improvement and training. Hi3D publishes no exact API retention period or per-task deletion endpoint; its policy provides account and personal-data deletion rights. OpenMates requires your confirmation before first use.

heading.text: Fitness search (only when you use the fitness skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the fitness app's Urban Sports location or class search skills. We query public logged-out discovery pages and do not send OpenMates user identifiers or Urban Sports credentials.

Urban Sports Club powers fitness location and class availability search. Urban Sports Club receives your search query details such as city, address or coordinates, radius, dates, attendance mode, and plan filter, without OpenMates user identifiers.

We use Revolut Bank UAB (Lithuania, EU) as our receiving bank for SEPA bank transfers. When you choose to pay via bank transfer, we display our Revolut IBAN to you. Revolut notifies us via a cryptographically signed webhook when a transfer arrives. We do not send your personal data to Revolut — only the transaction reference, amount, and Revolut's own transaction ID are processed.

heading.text: Payment providers (only when you purchase credits)

description.text: These providers are only used when you purchase credits, subscribe to monthly auto top-up, or receive a refund. If you never make a purchase, none of your data is shared with them.

Stripe processes one-time credit purchases and monthly auto top-up subscriptions. We send Stripe your email address, a tokenized payment method (we never see your card number), billing address and VAT information when required for invoicing, and transaction metadata.

intro.text: Most of the providers below are only reached when you use a specific feature — for example, image generation providers are only used when you invoke an image skill. The groups below tell you exactly which providers are involved for each feature, so you can opt in or out of data sharing by choosing which features to use.

description.text: These providers are used for every user, regardless of which features you use. Using OpenMates at all means your data passes through them.
We use Vercel to host the static frontend of our website and web app. Vercel receives page requests and serves static assets.

We host all of our backend services — API servers, Directus CMS, Postgres database, Redis caches, S3-compatible object storage, and our self-hosted OpenObserve observability platform — on Hetzner infrastructure in the EU. OpenObserve runs on our own Hetzner servers and is not a third-party service; traces never leave the EU.

We use Brevo to send transactional email — account verification, password reset links, payment receipts, and credit notes — and, if you opt in, the OpenMates newsletter. If you are an existing OpenMates customer (i.e. you have completed a purchase), we may also send you occasional product announcements and service updates about OpenMates' own similar services under the existing-customer exception (§7 Abs. 3 UWG / ePrivacy Directive Art. 13(2)); you can object in Settings → Newsletter or via the one-click unsubscribe link in any such email. Brevo sees recipient email addresses and the content of the emails we send you.

We use IP-API to resolve IP addresses to approximate geolocation for abuse prevention, rate limiting, and regional compliance. The resolved country and city are used transiently and are not stored against your account.
Every image and video you upload is scanned by Sightengine for safety moderation before it is stored. Sightengine sees the image or video content.

We use api.video (EU company, France) to host and stream product demo and feature walkthrough videos shown on our website and web app. When you watch a video, your IP address and basic viewing data are processed by api.video. No user account identifiers are shared.

We host backend services, databases, caches, S3-compatible object storage, backups, and our self-hosted OpenObserve platform on Hetzner infrastructure in the EU. Hetzner processes TLS-encrypted service traffic and stores ciphertext. Uploads and recordings also pass through its infrastructure before our upload service encrypts them for durable storage. Encryption reduces what Hetzner can read at rest but does not remove Hetzner's role as an infrastructure processor.

heading.text: AI model providers (only when you use a model that routes through them)

description.text: OpenMates routes AI requests to different providers depending on which model you select. Before any message is sent to a provider in this group, your browser replaces real names, emails, and physical addresses with placeholders (see the "PII placeholder substitution" measure above). You can always see which provider a model uses in the model details panel in AI settings.
Mistral hosts its own family of models in the EU. Only used when you select a Mistral model. Mistral receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.

heading.text: AWS Bedrock (EU region, primary Claude path)

description.text: AWS Bedrock hosts Anthropic Claude models in its Frankfurt EU region. This is the primary path for Claude requests. AWS receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.

Anthropic's direct API is used as a fallback path for Claude models when AWS Bedrock is unreachable. Anthropic is based in the US and receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.
OpenAI processes requests for GPT-family models when you select one. OpenAI receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.

OpenRouter routes requests to several third-party models, including Cerebras-hosted models. It sees chat messages with PII placeholders substituted client-side and forwards them to the model host. If direct TypeSafe credentials are unavailable, or direct authentication, transport, or transient service failures occur, OpenRouter may also route TypeSafe Jev decisions using the same minimized decision inputs described below.

OpenMates primarily sends bounded decision requests directly to TypeSafe Jev on US-hosted services. Jev receives bounded recent chat context and candidate metadata to make internal routing, model-tier, skill, focus-mode, language, and safety decisions. It also checks external text for prompt injection. For optional search relevance ranking, it receives the stated relevance criteria, search parameters, and minimized candidate data from supported public searches. OpenMates does not send user identifiers, and Jev returns typed decisions rather than generated chat text. OpenRouter is used only as a fallback when direct credentials are unavailable, or direct authentication, transport, or transient service failures occur; it receives the same minimized decision inputs and forwards them to TypeSafe Jev.
Cerebras hosts some of the high-speed models routed through OpenRouter. Only used when you select a Cerebras-hosted model.
Google Gemini processes requests for Gemini-family models when you select one. Google receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.

Google Vertex AI Model-as-a-Service hosts third-party open models (such as DeepSeek) on Google infrastructure via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This is a separate service from Google Gemini: the model weights are third-party, but the inference runs on Google's servers. Only used when you select a MaaS-hosted model.

Together AI hosts third-party models such as Kimi K2.6 on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Only used when you select a Together-hosted model. Together receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side.

Groq is used server-side to sanitize external content (search results and scraped web pages) before it is included in AI responses. For audio.speak, Groq also receives the requested speech text without OpenMates user identifiers to approve or reject the request before ElevenLabs is called. Groq never learns which user requested each piece of content or speech sample.
Alibaba Cloud hosts Qwen-family models. Alibaba receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side only when you select an Alibaba-hosted model.
DeepSeek provides DeepSeek-family reasoning models. DeepSeek receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side only when you select a DeepSeek model.
Moonshot AI provides Kimi-family models. Moonshot receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side only when you select a Moonshot-hosted Kimi model.
Z.ai provides GLM-family models. Z.ai receives your chat messages with PII placeholders already substituted client-side only when you select a Z.ai model.

description_v2.text: OpenMates routes requests to these providers according to the model or provider-powered feature you use. Eligible typed chat messages use client-side placeholder substitution. Recordings, raw transcripts, uploaded files, reference images, connected-account content, and structured skill inputs are not covered unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Selectable models show their provider in AI settings.

description.text: Mistral processes eligible chat messages when you select a Mistral model and processes realtime or uploaded voice audio when you use audio transcription. Voice audio can contain personal or sensitive information and does not receive typed-message placeholder substitution. Mistral states that ordinary API inputs and outputs may be retained for 30 rolling days for abuse monitoring unless zero-data retention is activated; OpenMates does not promise zero-data retention for this path.

OpenAI processes eligible chat messages when you select a GPT-family model. It also receives image prompts, generation settings, and any reference images when you select GPT Image for generation or editing. Reference images are not covered by typed-message placeholder substitution.

Google's Gemini API processes eligible chat messages when you select a Gemini model. Gemini is also used to correct raw Mistral voice transcripts and create titles, and may process prompts, reference images, screenshots, or generated code for image generation or editing, Veo video generation, and screenshot-to-HTML conversion. These non-chat inputs do not receive typed-message placeholder substitution. Google's paid Gemini API terms say prompts and outputs are not used to improve its products, while its current abuse-monitoring documentation states that logged prompts, context, and outputs may be retained for 55 days.

heading.text: Image generation and editing (only when you use an image skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke an image generation or editing skill. If you never use the images app, none of your data is shared with them.
FAL hosts Flux image generation models used by the images.generate_draft skill. FAL receives your image generation prompts and, when editing, the source images you supply.

Recraft powers the images.generate and images.vectorize skills, producing vector and raster images and converting bitmaps to SVG. Recraft receives your prompts, style preferences, and — when vectorizing — your source images.
Black Forest Labs powers draft image generation via FLUX models. BFL receives your image generation prompts and, when editing, the source images you provide.

heading.text: Audio generation and speech (only when you use an audio generation skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke an audio generation or text-to-speech skill. If you never use the audio generation skills, none of your data is shared with them.

ElevenLabs powers audio.generate sound effects and audio.speak text-to-speech. ElevenLabs receives your sound-effect prompts or requested speech text, chosen OpenMates voice preset, accent, style, speed, output format, duration, and generation settings only when you invoke those skills. audio.speak text is checked by the Groq safeguard first; rejected requests are not sent to ElevenLabs and are not charged generation credits.

heading.text: Music generation (only when you use a music skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke a music generation skill. If you never use the music app, none of your data is shared with them.

Google Vertex AI hosts the Lyria models used by the music.generate skill. Google receives your music generation prompts, optional lyrics, style preferences, and generation settings only when you ask OpenMates to generate music or background music.

heading.text: Code and developer tools (only when you use code skills)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke a code app skill, such as searching public repositories, running code in an isolated sandbox, creating a generated application that auto-starts a short screenshot preview, or explicitly starting a generated application live preview. If you never use the code app, none of your data is shared with them.
GitHub powers the code app's repository search skill. GitHub receives public repository search queries without an OpenMates user identifier.
Context7 powers the code app's documentation lookup skill. Context7 receives library names and documentation questions without an OpenMates user identifier.

E2B runs selected code embeds, generated application previews, and Remotion video renders inside isolated sandboxes. E2B receives the code or generated application/Remotion files and assets needed to run or render the result, runtime inputs, preview/render logs, and execution output needed to display the sandbox result. This sharing happens when you explicitly run code, create a generated application that auto-starts a short screenshot preview, start/resume an application live preview, or when a Remotion video render auto-starts after the assistant closes an explicit remotion code fence.

heading.text: Web, search, and content retrieval (only when you use a web or search skill)

description.text: These providers are used only when you use web, media, icon, or domain search and reading skills. They may receive your query, requested URL, or domain name, but no OpenMates user identifier.
Brave Search powers the web, videos, and news search skills. Brave sees the text of your search queries and your country and language preferences for localized results, but no user identifier.
Firecrawl powers the web read skill, scraping and extracting content from web pages you ask about. Firecrawl sees the URL you requested and the full content of the scraped page.

Iconify powers the design.search_icons skill. Iconify sees icon search queries and the icon collection/name needed to fetch SVG previews, but no OpenMates user identifier. OpenMates fetches Iconify data server-side and clients do not call Iconify directly.

domain_fallback.text: For domain searches, Webshare is a fallback when the direct Gandi request fails. It sees the Gandi host and connection metadata, but cannot read the HTTPS-encrypted domain query or an OpenMates user identifier.

description.text: Webshare provides a rotating proxy for requests to services that would otherwise block us. We route YouTube transcript requests (for the videos get-transcript skill) and doctor appointment searches (for the health search-appointments skill — see Group H) through Webshare. Webshare sees the URLs we route through it.

Gandi receives domain names or search keywords, country and currency when you use Hosting's domain search. OpenMates sends requests from its server over HTTPS without your OpenMates user identifier or Gandi credentials. Prices are indicative; no registration is performed.
Google Maps powers the places search skill. Google sees the text of your place queries and an approximate location for localized results, but no user identifier.

Geoapify is used by the Maps search skill to enrich Google Places results with OpenStreetMap-backed amenity details such as air conditioning, internet access, wheelchair access, toilets, outdoor seating, diet, and payment hints when available. Geoapify receives only the place query or matching data needed for enrichment, such as approximate coordinates, category/filter parameters, and Geoapify place IDs, without OpenMates user identifiers.

Wikimedia is contacted only after you explicitly activate Wiki search. It receives the article query and language, and later the canonical title selected for summary retrieval. Requests are sent by the OpenMates server without your OpenMates user identifier, chat ID, or client IP address.
YouTube is queried when you ask OpenMates to retrieve a transcript for a YouTube video. YouTube receives video URLs and requested transcript language preferences without an OpenMates user identifier.

When you request reverse-image search, SerpAPI brokers the request to Google Lens. SerpAPI and Google receive a short-lived public URL to a decrypted copy of the selected image and any optional text refinement. The URL expires, and no OpenMates user identifier is included.

heading.text: Travel (only when you use a travel skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke a travel skill — flight search, hotel search, or flight tracking. If you never use the travel app, none of your data is shared with them.

SerpAPI powers flight and hotel search via its Google Flights and Google Hotels endpoints. SerpAPI receives your search queries — origin, destination, dates, and preferences — without a user identifier.
Flightradar24 provides real flight track data when you ask about a specific flight number. It receives IATA flight numbers and departure dates without a user identifier.
Deutsche Bahn provides train connection results when you search for rail routes. Deutsche Bahn receives origin, destination, and date search details without an OpenMates user identifier.

Flix provides intercity bus and rail connection results when you search for FlixBus or FlixTrain routes. Flix receives origin, destination, and date search details without an OpenMates user identifier.

SerpAPI powers flight, hotel, Amazon product, and Google Lens reverse-image searches. It receives the relevant query and localization filters without an OpenMates user identifier. Reverse-image search also sends a short-lived URL to a decrypted copy of the selected image and any optional refinement query.

Transitous receives origin and destination stations or locations, travel date and time, transport modes, and route options for supported European public-transport routing. Requests are server-side without an OpenMates user identifier. Transitous states that request URLs and server request metadata are retained for up to two days.

heading.text: Events (only when you use the events skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the events search skill. The specific set of providers called depends on the city and event type you search for.
Meetup powers event search for community events. Meetup receives your search queries — city, category, dates — without a user identifier.
Luma powers event search for tech, creative, and community events. Luma receives your search queries without a user identifier.
Resident Advisor powers event search for electronic music events. RA receives your search queries without a user identifier.
Eventbrite receives the event query, city, category, dates, and requested result count for public event search and page retrieval. Requests are sent server-side without an OpenMates user identifier.

Siegessäule receives the date range and, when applicable, a matching event section or category for Berlin LGBTQ+ event listings. Requests are routed through Webshare without an OpenMates user identifier; unmatched free-text filtering happens locally.

Berliner Philharmoniker receives the concert query, date filters, tags, and requested result count when you search its public calendar. Requests are sent server-side without an OpenMates user identifier.

heading.text: Health appointment search (only when you use the health skill)

description.text: These upstream services are reached through the Webshare rotating proxy (see Group E) only when you invoke the health app's appointment search skill. The queries you send — for example "dermatologist in Berlin next Tuesday" — are transmitted without user identifiers, but the content of the query itself can imply a health concern. By invoking the skill you consent to this processing under GDPR Art. 9(2)(a) (explicit consent for special-category data).
Doctolib lists doctors and specialists across supported EU regions. We query Doctolib for available appointments matching your criteria, routed through the Webshare proxy, without a user identifier.
Jameda lists doctors and specialists across Germany. We query Jameda for available appointments matching your criteria, routed through the Webshare proxy, without a user identifier.

heading.text: Shopping (only when you use the shopping skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the shopping search skill for live product and price lookups.
REWE's product catalogue is queried for live product and price data when you search German grocery items. REWE receives your search queries without a user identifier.
Amazon's product catalogue is queried for live product and price data. Amazon receives your search queries without a user identifier.

Stoffe.de receives the product query, category, sorting, pagination, and compatible shipping-country filters for fabric, sewing-supply, and pattern searches. Requests are sent server-side without an OpenMates user identifier.

heading.text: Nutrition (only when you use the recipe search skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the nutrition recipe search skill. They receive recipe search queries and selected dietary filters without a user identifier.
Edamam's Recipe Search API is queried when you search for recipes. Edamam receives the recipe query and selected dietary or nutrition filters without a user identifier.

heading.text: Electronics (only when you use the electronics skill)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the electronics component search skill for live component and reference-design lookups.

TI WEBENCH is queried for power converter component candidates and reference design summaries. Texas Instruments receives the electrical requirements you search for, such as input voltage, output voltage, output current, temperature, isolation, and optimization goal, without a user identifier.

heading.text: Mail (only when you use mail skills)

description.text: This provider is only used when you connect or invoke mail skills against a connected mailbox. If you never use the mail app, none of your data is shared with it.

When you run the Proton Mail Bridge connector, OpenMates sends mail requests to your local CLI process, which talks to Proton Bridge on your device. Proton receives the mailbox data needed to serve those Bridge requests. Your Proton Bridge IMAP/SMTP credentials stay local and are not sent to OpenMates servers. Outgoing message content is sent only if you explicitly start the connector with write access and send mail.

heading.text: Home and housing (only when you use housing search)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the home app's housing search skill. If you never search for housing, none of your data is shared with them.
ImmoScout24 is queried when you search German housing listings. ImmoScout24 receives housing search queries, locations, filters, and listing pages requested without an OpenMates user identifier.

Kleinanzeigen is queried when you search German classified housing listings. Kleinanzeigen receives housing search queries, locations, filters, and listing pages requested without an OpenMates user identifier.

WG-Gesucht is queried when you search German shared-apartment or rental listings. WG-Gesucht receives housing search queries, locations, filters, and listing pages requested without an OpenMates user identifier.

heading.text: Community and developer channels (only if you choose to use them)

description.text: These providers are only involved if you choose to join our community or developer channels. You can use OpenMates without ever touching them.

If you join the OpenMates community Discord server, Discord will see anything you post on its platform, plus your Discord username and whatever data Discord itself collects per its own privacy policy. We have no control over what Discord does with that data.

admin_access.text: OpenMates administrators with Discord server admin rights can read all messages posted in the OpenMates Discord server. Do not share sensitive information on Discord.

heading.text: Social media (only when you use social media skills)

description.text: These providers are only used when you invoke the social media app's get-posts or search skills. They receive public profile, page, or search queries without an OpenMates user identifier.
Reddit is queried when you fetch or search public Reddit posts. Reddit receives subreddit names, public post URLs, and search queries without an OpenMates user identifier.
Bluesky is queried when you fetch or search public Bluesky posts. Bluesky receives handles and search queries without an OpenMates user identifier.
Mastodon is queried when you fetch public Mastodon profile posts. The relevant Mastodon server receives profile identifiers or public profile URLs without an OpenMates user identifier.
These providers are used only when you search the public 3D model catalog or invoke a 3D model generation skill.
Printables receives the 3D model search query and requested result limit when you search its public catalog. The request is sent server-side without an OpenMates user identifier.
These providers are used only after you connect an external account and authorize access. OpenMates requests the scopes needed for the action and stores durable credential material encrypted.

After you connect Google Calendar, OpenMates exchanges the OAuth authorization code and stores refresh or access tokens encrypted. Authorized actions may access calendar IDs, names, time zones, event IDs, titles, descriptions, locations, dates, and attendee email addresses. OpenMates reads, creates, updates, or deletes only within the scopes and action you authorize.
This provider is used only when you explicitly request public company financial information.
The SEC receives the explicit company name, ticker, or CIK and the filing or period fields needed for a public-company lookup. Requests are sent server-side without an OpenMates user identifier.

A named place is first geocoded by Open-Meteo. Germany forecasts then use Bright Sky's DWD-derived data; forecasts elsewhere use Open-Meteo. These services receive location and forecast parameters without an OpenMates user identifier.

Open-Meteo receives a place name and language for geocoding, and coordinates, date range, time zone, and requested weather fields for global forecasts outside the Germany-specific path. Requests exclude OpenMates user identifiers. Open-Meteo states that API logs may contain coordinates and are deleted after 90 days.

Bright Sky receives coordinates, date range, time zone, radar radius, and requested weather fields for Germany forecasts and rain radar using public DWD-derived data. Requests exclude OpenMates user identifiers. Bright Sky does not publish a standalone privacy notice, so the link points to its official service documentation.

overview.text: This privacy policy explains what happens to your data when you use our website and web application. We are committed to transparency regarding data handling and work with various service providers to deliver our services.

website_vs_webapp.text: OpenMates (https://openmates.org) serves as both our informational website and web application. All visitors access OpenMates through Vercel. When you sign up and use our AI features, your data is also processed by our backend services (hosted on Hetzner) and various AI providers as described below.

description.text: Our website and web app (static content) is hosted using Vercel's platform (US company). When you visit our website or web app, your request is processed by Vercel's servers. Vercel may collect technical information including IP addresses, browser type and version, basic access logs, performance data, and other standard server logs.

intro.text: The following services are used when you sign up and use OpenMates AI features:

description.text: Our web application's backend services, databases, and file storage are hosted on Hetzner's infrastructure (EU company, EU servers). This includes web app backend hosting, all backend processing, database hosting, and S3 file hosting.
We use IP-API (EU company) for IP address geolocation to determine approximate geographic location for security and localization purposes in the web application.

We use Brevo (EU company) to send emails. This includes account-related transactional emails (e.g., account verification, security alerts), newsletter emails if you subscribed, and — for existing OpenMates customers — occasional product announcements and service updates under the existing-customer exception (§7 Abs. 3 UWG / ePrivacy Directive Art. 13(2)). Your email address and the email content are shared with Brevo for delivery.
We use Sightengine (EU company) for moderation of uploaded images and videos in the web application to ensure content compliance with our terms of service.
We use Stripe (US company) for payment processing for purchases made in the web application, ensuring secure handling of payment information.
We use Mistral AI (EU company) for LLM requests processing in the web application to process some of your chat requests and provide AI-powered responses.

We use AWS Bedrock (US company, EU servers) to access Anthropic's Claude models for LLM requests processing in the web application, handling some of your chat requests and providing AI-powered responses.

We use OpenRouter (US company, US servers) as a gateway to access multiple large-language-model providers. When your chat request is routed via OpenRouter, it may process your prompts and responses to deliver the requested AI output.
We may use Cerebras (US company, US servers) as a language model provider through OpenRouter to process some of your chat requests and provide AI-generated responses.

heading.text: 3.10 Brave Search (Web, Videos, and News Search)

description.text: We use Brave Search (US company) for web search, video search, and news search in the web application. When you use these search skills, your search queries and preferences (such as country and language settings) are sent to Brave Search to provide you with search results. Brave sees the content of what you search for (your search queries), but all data is shared without user identifiers - Brave does not know which specific user made each search. This data sharing only occurs when you actively use the web search, videos search, or news search skills.

We use Webshare as a third-party service for making network requests to external services in the web application. When you use the videos get transcript, health get appointments, or events search skills, the relevant request URLs are routed through Webshare to the respective services. Webshare sees which URLs are requested, but all data is shared without user identifiers — Webshare does not know which specific user made each request. This data sharing only occurs when you actively use these skills.

We use Google (US company) for maps search and LLM requests processing in the web application. When you use the maps search skill, your place search queries are sent to Google Maps Platform to provide you with place information - Google sees the content of what places you search for. We also use Google GenAI for LLM requests processing, which processes your chat messages and prompts - Google GenAI sees the content of your chat messages and prompts. All data is shared without user identifiers - Google does not know which specific user made each search or sent each message. This data sharing only occurs when you actively use the maps search skill or when your chat requests are processed via Google GenAI.

We use Firecrawl (US company) for web scraping in the web application. When you use the web read skill, the URLs of web pages you request to be scraped are sent to Firecrawl, which scrapes and returns the content of these web pages. Firecrawl sees and processes the full content of websites you request to read, but all data is shared without user identifiers - Firecrawl does not know which specific user requested each web page. This data sharing only occurs when you actively use the web read skill.

We use Groq (US company) for LLM requests processing when you use skills that retrieve external data, such as search results from Brave or website content from Firecrawl. Groq sees and processes the actual content of search results and scraped web pages to sanitize them before they are included in your chat responses. All data is shared without user identifiers - Groq does not know which specific user requested the processing of each piece of content. This data sharing only occurs when you use skills that retrieve external data and that content needs to be processed.

When you request real flight track data using the "Get flight track" skill, we query Flightradar24 to retrieve historical GPS track data for completed flights. Flightradar24 receives the flight number and departure date. No personal data is shared.

intro.text: We implement various security measures to protect your account and data in the web application:

purpose.text: To enhance account security, prevent fraudulent access, and distinguish between new and recognized devices during login and session validation, we collect User-Agent strings (browser, OS, device type information) and IP addresses (used temporarily to derive approximate geo-location like country/city, then discarded from the device record).

storage.text: A unique, stable hash is generated based on a combination of the collected signals. This hash is the only value stored in the device record. Browser/OS type and derived country code may be used transiently for risk assessment and notifications but are not stored with the device record. Raw IP addresses are NOT stored as part of the device record itself.

ip_logging.text: For security monitoring and abuse prevention, IP addresses associated with failed login attempts (invalid password or 2FA code) may be logged with limited retention. In addition, certain security/compliance events (e.g., successful backup-code logins) may be logged with IP for audit purposes. IP addresses are also used for rate limiting login attempts.

heading.text: 5. Data Categories We Collect and Process

intro.text: We collect and process the following categories of data to operate and secure our services:

account.text: Account: Email address, username/display name, profile image, locale, and security settings (e.g., 2FA enabled). Email and username are encrypted with your key before storage. We also keep a separate server-side Vault-encrypted copy of your verified email address for mandatory account lifecycle notices, such as account verification, security alerts, and deletion reminders. Passwords are stored as salted hashes.

usage.text: Usage: Server logs, event timestamps, feature usage, error logs, and device recognition identifiers (hashed). IP addresses may be temporarily processed for security, rate limiting, and anonymous free-usage budget checks. Anonymous free usage uses a first-party random local identifier and sends only a server-side HMAC-hashed form for per-identity abuse limits.

content.text: Content: Chat messages, prompts, attachments, and uploaded images/videos necessary to deliver the service (subject to moderation where applicable). Anonymous free-usage chats stay local-only and encrypted with per-chat keys before signup; they are uploaded only if you sign up and promote them into account sync.

payments.text: Payments: Payment method tokens, transaction IDs, billing address and VAT information as required for invoicing (processed primarily by Stripe). We do not store full card numbers.

newsletter.text: Newsletter: If you choose to subscribe to our newsletter, we store your email address in encrypted form. Newsletter subscription is optional and separate from account creation — creating an account does not automatically subscribe you to the newsletter. If you are an OpenMates customer (i.e. you have completed a purchase), we may additionally send you occasional product announcements and service updates about OpenMates' own similar services under the existing-customer exception (§7 Abs. 3 UWG / ePrivacy Directive Art. 13(2)). You can object to this at any time in Settings → Newsletter or via the one-click unsubscribe link in any such email, without affecting your account.

stability_logs.text: Stability Logs: To diagnose technical errors, anonymized browser console logs (error messages, component status, connection events) are collected from authenticated users and stored for up to 48 hours. storage_expiry.text: Where unpaid personal-storage expiry is enabled, an unpaid storage episode may lead to removal of the affected personal files only after four weekly warning emails confirmed as delivered by our email provider, at least 7 days apart. We check payment again immediately before removal. The affected files are fixed for that warned episode. We select complete personal file units from that set, oldest first, removing only enough to bring eligible usage within the free allowance. Team or shared files, active files, the sole remaining offline recovery copy, files whose ownership or removal safety is uncertain, and files covered by later paid storage periods are protected. If no safe set of complete eligible units can bring usage within the allowance, we remove nothing and waive nothing. Only after we verify the affected files have been removed and eligible usage is at or below the free allowance do we waive the unpaid storage invoices included in that warning episode. Their status becomes waived_on_expiry, not paid; this waiver makes no credit debit. Later debt that was not included in the warnings and paid storage periods are unaffected. Logical removal creates content-free regional deletion markers and queues physical object deletion only after the last retained references have been removed; it does not promise immediate physical erasure. Backup and historical-record retention remain as described in our Privacy Policy. Where unpaid Team-storage expiry is enabled, we notify the current Team owner and admins. Each of the four weekly warning rounds counts only after our email provider confirms delivery to every required recipient. The same minimum warning intervals and expiry dates apply. We select complete, specifically warned Team file units, oldest first, removing only enough to restore that Team's separate free allowance. Active work, sole recovery copies, required references outside the selected units, uncertain ownership or removal safety, and later-paid data remain protected. We recheck the Team wallet, current membership, notice delivery, usage and references before removal. If no safe set can restore the allowance, we remove and waive nothing. Only verified removal restoring the allowance can waive that Team's warned unpaid episode; later debt and paid periods remain unaffected.

summary.text: OpenMates is designed so that most of your data is encrypted on your device before it reaches our servers. This is **not** end-to-end encryption: our servers briefly decrypt your content in memory to run AI responses, render invoices, and deliver reminders. But we never write decrypted content to disk, logs, or traces, and when you delete your account we destroy the encryption key that protects your data — cryptographically shredding every encrypted field we still hold.

intro.text: These answers summarize the most important privacy points in plain language. The detailed policy and provider tables below explain the same topics in more depth.

question.text: Can OpenMates employees read my private chats?

answer.text: Private chats are not routinely reviewed by OpenMates employees, and we do not provide a normal admin screen for browsing private chat content. However, OpenMates is not a strict end-to-end encrypted or zero-knowledge system: relevant content can be processed temporarily in server memory when you ask for an AI response or use a feature that needs server processing.

question.text: How are my chats protected?

answer.text: Your saved chat history is encrypted on your device before it is stored or synced. OpenMates does not provide staff with a normal admin tool to browse private chats, and decrypted chat content is not intended to be written to databases, backups, logs, or traces. When you ask for an AI response or use a server-powered feature, OpenMates may temporarily process the relevant decrypted content in server memory so the request can work. This means hosted OpenMates is privacy-protective, but not a strict zero-knowledge or device-only system.

question.text: What is the recent AI context cache?

answer.text: To make follow-up responses fast, OpenMates may keep a short-lived, server-readable AI context cache for recent chats, currently designed around the last 3 chats. This cache is encrypted with server-side Vault encryption, but OpenMates servers can decrypt it while processing your request. If the cache is missing, the server may ask your active client to resend the needed decrypted context and cache it temporarily again.

question.text: Where are my chats stored, and how are they protected?

answer.text: Saved chats are stored on OpenMates infrastructure as encrypted data. Chat content, titles, summaries, tags, app settings, memories, reminders, and sensitive profile fields are designed to be encrypted before durable storage. Persistent storage, backups, and sync caches should not contain readable chat text.

question.text: Do third-party AI providers see my messages?

answer.text: Yes, when you choose a model or use a feature powered by a third-party provider, the content needed to process that request may be sent to that provider. OpenMates tries to reduce exposure by replacing recognized personal details and secrets with placeholders before sending, but anything not detected may be sent as typed.

question.text: Are my chats used to train AI models?

answer.text: OpenMates does not use your private chats to train OpenMates-owned AI models. For third-party providers, the answer depends on the provider. Most audited chat-model providers state that they do not train on API customer data, or only train if the customer opts in. Some image or 3D generation providers have broader or limited-use policies. The provider-by-provider training table below lists the status, source document, and last verification date.

question.text: Does placeholder protection make sensitive data safe to send?

answer.text: No. Placeholder protection reduces risk, but it is not a guarantee. It works best for recognized personal data, saved privacy-profile values, and common secret patterns. It may miss typos, unusual formats, context-only sensitive information, other people's personal data, or sensitive topics that are not technically identifiable as personal data.

question.text: What data appears in logs or diagnostics?

answer.text: OpenMates is designed so chat content is not written to logs or traces. Application logs and telemetry include redaction and filtering for authentication headers, cookies, tokens, passwords, emails, IP addresses, and chat content. Browser stability logs are sanitized, use temporary session identifiers, and can be disabled in privacy settings.

question.text: What happens when I delete my account or chats?

answer.text: When you delete chats or your account, OpenMates deletes the corresponding data according to the retention rules below. For account deletion, OpenMates also destroys encryption keys so any remaining encrypted data in backups or caches becomes unreadable ciphertext. Some records may remain for legal or operational reasons, such as invoices, payment records, audit logs, third-party provider logs, or short-lived encrypted backups.

question.text: What does open source mean for my privacy?

answer.text: Open source means the OpenMates software code is public and can be inspected by others. It does not mean your private data is public. Your chats, account data, settings, memories, uploads, and billing data are not published on GitHub. The code is public; your personal data is not.

question.text: Is OpenMates suitable for sensitive topics?

answer.text: OpenMates is privacy-conscious, but it is not a zero-knowledge or device-only system. It is reasonable for everyday private AI use when you avoid unnecessary personal details. For highly sensitive legal, medical, financial, business-confidential, or safety-critical topics, be careful about what you enter and which model or provider you use.

question.text: What if I have the highest privacy requirements?

answer.text: If you have very high privacy requirements, consider the [self-hosting edition](https://github.com/glowingkitty/OpenMates/blob/dev/docs/self-hosting/setup.md) of OpenMates with local or offline AI models instead of third-party AI providers. This gives you more control over infrastructure, model choice, logs, backups, and provider exposure. It requires technical experience, ongoing maintenance, secure server administration, and enough hardware for useful local AI inference. Self-hosting does not automatically make everything private: you still need to secure the server, backups, secrets, network access, logs, and any external providers you enable.

question.text: Do third-party providers receive my content?

answer.text: Yes, when you choose a model or use a provider-powered feature, the content needed for that request may be sent to the provider. Eligible typed chat messages use client-side placeholder substitution for recognized personal details and secrets. Anything not detected may be sent as typed, and the protection does not cover voice recordings, raw transcripts, uploaded files, reference images, calendar content, or structured skill inputs unless a feature explicitly says otherwise.

question.text: What happens when I record audio?

answer.text: Audio travels over TLS through the OpenMates backend hosted by Hetzner and is sent to Mistral for transcription. Realtime audio is streamed; uploaded recordings are encrypted by our upload service before durable storage and decrypted only in server memory for transcription. The raw transcript is then sent to Google Gemini to correct obvious transcription errors and create a title. Audio and raw transcripts do not receive the placeholder substitution used for eligible typed chat messages. OpenMates stores recordings and transcripts as encrypted account content, but Mistral and Google may retain API request data under their own policies.

Saved chats, artifact history, settings, and memories are stored as ciphertext. PostgreSQL holds their records; these records are encrypted for authorized clients. Uploaded files and recordings are kept separately as encrypted objects in S3. A separate short-lived AI context cache is encrypted with server-side Vault keys and can be read by OpenMates servers while processing your request. A pending assistant response sealed to a client public key for offline recovery remains available until an authorized client verifies and confirms its normal client-encrypted save, or the related chat or account is deleted. Large sealed responses may be stored in regional S3 object storage. Expiry of a retry lease or the AI working cache alone does not remove the pending sealed copy. The server cannot rebuild missing readable AI context from client-encrypted history without an authorized client.

When you delete a chat or your account, OpenMates removes records under that deletion's authority and schedules removal of unshared S3 objects in the configured regions. Encrypted regional copies may remain while verified physical deletion completes. Account key destruction also makes remaining content encrypted with that account key unreadable. Content retained by another authorized owner or Team is not erased by one member's account deletion. Invoices, payment records, audit logs, and provider-held data may remain for the periods described below. Content-free deletion markers may also remain as described in the retention section.

Deletion of a chat or account removes its current records under that deletion’s authority and schedules removal of unshared regional S3 objects. Encrypted regional copies can remain while verified physical deletion completes. Earlier database revision and activity records can still retain account-profile details or encrypted chat and artifact snapshots after the current records are deleted. Those historical records are separate from content-free deletion markers and currently have no automatic expiry. Account-key destruction makes only content protected solely by that key unreadable. Content retained by another authorized owner or Team, financial records, and provider-held data can also remain as described below.

intro.text: We rely on six technical measures to protect your data. Each is verifiable in our open-source code and maps to a specific GDPR obligation.

description.text: Your chat content, titles, summaries, tags, per-chat keys, app settings and memories, reminders, and sensitive profile fields (encrypted username, auto-top-up email, 2FA secrets) are encrypted in your browser before being sent to our servers. The browser uses a key derived from your login credential; our servers reject writes that contain anything but ciphertext. This is *not* end-to-end encryption — our servers can decrypt your content in memory when they need to (for AI responses, invoice rendering, reminder delivery). The difference from end-to-end encryption is that decryption happens transiently in process memory and the plaintext is never persisted to disk, logs, or traces.

heading.text: PII placeholder substitution before AI calls

description.text: Before any message is sent to a third-party AI model, your browser scans your message for real names, email addresses, and physical addresses that you have saved in your privacy settings (or that match common patterns) and replaces any matches with neutral placeholders (for example [USER_0]). The mapping back to your real values is stored encrypted with your key and is never decrypted on our servers. **Important limitation:** this substitution only protects personal data that our client-side detector actually recognizes — typically the values you have explicitly saved in your privacy settings and values highlighted in the message field before you send. Anything the detector does not recognize (typos of your own name, uncommon address formats, other people's personal data, sensitive topics that are not formally PII) will be transmitted as you typed it. Please treat every message as you would treat a note passed to a third-party AI provider and be cautious with personal data.

heading.text: Encrypted at rest, decrypted only in memory

description.text: Our PostgreSQL database, Redis caches, S3 object storage, and backup snapshots hold only ciphertext for any field containing user content. When our servers need to read your content to run an AI response, render an invoice, or deliver a reminder, decryption happens transiently in process memory and is discarded immediately after. Key material is released on demand by HashiCorp Vault and never stored in raw form outside it.

Your user ID is stored in most database tables as a SHA-256 hash rather than as a direct reference. Login uses a zero-knowledge password verification flow: we verify that you know your password without ever learning it. API-key device records anonymize the IP address to its first two octets before encryption, so we can recognize a device without storing a precise location.

When you delete your account we destroy your HashiCorp Vault Transit key in addition to removing your rows from our database. Any encrypted field still sitting in a backup, cache, or running process becomes mathematically unrecoverable ciphertext at that moment — cryptographic erasure on top of row-level deletion.

Our internal tracing pipeline (OpenTelemetry) replaces your user ID with a hash that rotates every 24 hours, strips authentication headers and cookies from every span, and redacts chat content before any trace leaves the backend. Our web analytics use a server-side beacon with no cookies and no stored individual identifiers. We do not use Google Analytics, Plausible, PostHog, or any third-party analytics platform.

intro.text: Below are the privacy promises we make to every user. Each one is backed by code in our open-source repository and verified by automated tests. When the enforcing code changes, a registry-linked check reminds us to rerun those tests before release.

description.text: Your chats, settings, and memories are encrypted on your device with AES-256-GCM before they leave your browser. The server stores only ciphertext on disk, in caches, and in backups. This is not end-to-end encryption: when a server-side task needs to read content (to run an AI response, render an invoice, or deliver a reminder), it decrypts in memory via HashiCorp Vault and discards the plaintext immediately after use.
Your email address is stored only as ciphertext. The server decrypts it transiently in memory during login, billing, and notification delivery, and never writes plaintext to disk or logs.

heading.text: No third-party tracking cookies or analytics

description.text: We do not use Google Analytics, Plausible, PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Segment, or any other third-party analytics platform. Our telemetry is server-side, cookie-free, and contains no individually stored identifiers. A pre-edit check in our repository blocks the introduction of analytics SDKs.

heading.text: Personal information never reaches AI providers

description.text: Before any message is sent to an AI provider, your browser detects 32 categories of personal data — emails, phone numbers, credit card numbers, API keys, and more — and replaces them with placeholders like `[EMAIL_com]`. The substitution map is encrypted with your chat key so only your devices can restore the original values.

Our internal tracing pipeline (OpenTelemetry) strips authentication headers, cookies, and database statements from every span, and pseudonymises your user ID with a salt that rotates every 24 hours. Regular users never have their raw identifiers in telemetry.
When you delete your account, the first step destroys your encryption keys. Any residual ciphertext in backups, caches, or audit logs is rendered permanently unreadable — no key, no content.

description_v2.text: On account deletion, OpenMates destroys the account-controlled encryption keys. Residual ciphertext protected only by those keys becomes unreadable. Shared content retained by another authorized owner or Team, and records held under separate legal authority, can remain.

description.text: We store password and backup-code verifiers as Argon2 hashes. Plaintext passwords are never persisted to disk, never written to logs, and never recoverable — even by us.

heading.text: No card numbers ever touch our servers

description.text: Payments flow directly from your browser to Stripe. We store only provider tokens and customer identifiers. We never see, receive, or persist full card numbers, security codes, or bank account details.

heading.text: Logs are scrubbed of sensitive data

description.text: Every log line passes through a redaction filter that strips email addresses, IP addresses, bearer tokens, and password values. Compliance logs preserve pseudonymous user IDs but remove all other personal data.

Two layers protect your conversations from malicious content in web pages, files, and URLs you reference. Invisible Unicode characters are stripped first, then a dedicated safety model detects semantic injection attempts and blocks or replaces high-risk content before it reaches your assistant.

heading.text: Your conversations are not used to train AI models

description.text: All AI chat providers we use (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Google Gemini, Google Vertex AI, Together AI, Groq, Cerebras, and OpenRouter) have explicit no-training clauses in their terms — your conversations are never used to fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise train AI models. For image generation, Recraft has a training opt-out which we have activated. fal.ai (used for draft image generation) may use anonymized, aggregated derivatives of prompts for model improvement under their standard API terms; no full opt-out is available outside an enterprise contract. A per-provider audit with verbatim policy quotes and verification dates is published in our open-source repository.

heading.text: The web app never loads external images or scripts

description.text: Every external image, favicon, or preview shown in the app is fetched through our own preview.openmates.org proxy — the originating website never sees your IP address. The only third-party script the web app loads is the Stripe payment SDK needed to process a purchase, and only when you explicitly open the payment flow. There is no ad network, tag manager, CDN font loader, or third-party analytics library.

heading.text: The command-line tool never asks for your password

description.text: The OpenMates CLI never prompts you for your email, password, 2FA code, or any other login credential. Authentication uses a browser-based pair-auth handshake: the CLI shows a QR code and URL, you approve the session in your logged-in web browser, and you type a short 6-character binding PIN back into the CLI to confirm. Your credentials never pass through the terminal.

heading.text: Every claim on this page is independently auditable

description.text: OpenMates is open source. Every promise above is backed by code you can read, tests you can run, and architecture documents you can audit in our public repository. Our privacy-promises registry links each claim to the exact files that enforce it.

heading.text: Structured chat data is encrypted before sync

description.text: Structured chat data, settings, and memories are encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM before sync, and the server stores ciphertext on disk, in caches, and in backups. Uploaded files and recordings instead travel to our backend over TLS and are encrypted by the upload service before durable storage. This is not end-to-end encryption; server-side tasks decrypt relevant content transiently in memory when needed to provide a requested feature.

heading.text: Recognized personal data is replaced in eligible typed chat

description.text: Before an eligible typed chat message is sent to an AI provider, your browser detects supported categories of personal data and secrets and replaces recognized values with placeholders. The substitution map is encrypted with your chat key. Detection can miss data, and this protection does not cover voice audio, raw transcripts, uploaded files, reference images, connected-account content, or structured skill inputs unless a feature explicitly says otherwise.

heading.text: What survives account deletion — and why

intro.text: When you delete your account we destroy your encryption key and remove your rows from our database. A small number of things are retained for limited, legally justified reasons:

heading.text: Financial records and financial compliance logs (up to 10 years)

description.text: Invoices, credit notes, and financial compliance log entries are retained for up to 10 years under GDPR Art. 17(3)(b) — legal obligation (German tax and commercial law, AO §147 and HGB §257). The retained records contain only transaction metadata, an invoice number, and a user identifier — not chat content or any other personal data.

description_v2.text: Invoices, credit notes and financial audit entries can remain after account deletion. The current storage configuration uses up to ten years; statutory German periods vary by record type, generally eight years for invoices and accounting vouchers and ten years for accounting books and annual accounts. Financial records can contain billing identity details, transaction metadata, invoice numbers and user identifiers. They are separate from chat content. GDPR Article 17(3)(b) applies where retention is required by law.

description.text: Authentication and data-access audit logs are retained for 2 years under BSI §34 BDSG (German security audit obligations). These logs contain timestamp, user identifier, event type, and status — no content.

description_v2.text: Authentication and data-access audit logs are currently configured for up to two years for security, fraud prevention and accountability. They can contain timestamps, user identifiers, event types and status. Their configured retention is not a general statutory two-year requirement.

description_v3.text: Authentication and data-access audit logs can contain timestamps, user identifiers, event types and status. No enforced automatic two-year expiry for historical database revision and activity records is currently in place. That history can contain prior record snapshots and is described separately below; financial retention follows the applicable record-specific rules.

heading.text: Logs retained by third-party AI providers

description.text: Each AI provider we send your prompts to (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Together, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras) retains its own request logs for trust-and-safety windows independent of OpenMates — typically 30 days. We cannot reach into their systems to delete your data. The PII placeholder substitution described in "How we protect your data" above limits what is in those logs in the first place — the providers see only placeholders, not your real names or addresses.

OpenTelemetry spans from our internal tracing pipeline are retained for up to 30 days for operational debugging. User IDs in traces use a hash that rotates every 24 hours, so traces older than one day cannot be joined back to a specific user. Chat content is never included in traces.

heading.text: Your own encrypted data backups (60 days)

description.text: Ciphertext backups of your own data exports live in S3 for 60 days via a lifecycle rule, so you can retrieve an export if your device is lost. Because we destroyed your encryption key when you deleted your account, we cannot decrypt these backups either — they are effectively inert ciphertext until they expire.

heading.text: Logs retained by third-party AI providers

description.text: AI providers retain request logs under their own policies, independently of OpenMates, and we cannot delete data from their systems. Retention is provider-specific; for example, Mistral states 30 rolling days for ordinary API input and output unless zero-data retention is active, while Google's current Gemini abuse-monitoring documentation states 55 days for logged prompts, context, and outputs. Eligible typed chat uses client-side placeholder substitution, which reduces exposure but may miss data and does not cover voice audio, raw transcripts, uploaded or reference files, connected-account content, or structured skill inputs unless a feature explicitly says otherwise.

title.text: OpenMates v0.10: New apps, skills, providers & learning tools

description.text: More useful things to do with OpenMates

message.text:
Hey there,

OpenMates v0.10 was mostly about making the product feel more useful in normal day-to-day situations: clearer answers, smoother chats, more apps and providers, and better ways to learn and get things done.

# ✨ The highlights

## 1. Wikipedia links directly inside answers

OpenMates can now highlight relevant Wikipedia topics directly inside assistant responses. When a concept is worth exploring further, you can click the highlighted term and quickly learn more without leaving the flow of the chat.

This is especially useful for learning, research, travel planning, history questions, science topics, or anything where the answer opens up a new rabbit hole.

## 2. Message highlights and comments

You can now highlight parts of assistant messages and keep notes on them. This makes longer answers much more useful: save the important paragraph, mark something you want to revisit, or keep a comment next to a specific claim or recommendation.

## 3. New apps and app skills

OpenMates got more useful app skills across everyday categories. Travel searches became more practical with train connections and booking links, Events gained more useful event sources, Code became better at understanding repositories, and several embed types became clearer and easier to act on.

Instead of only answering from the model's memory, OpenMates can increasingly use dedicated tools: search, compare, summarize, create files, inspect source material, and show structured results directly in the chat.

## 4. More providers for real-world results

v0.10 added and improved providers behind the scenes, for example for travel, events, payments, and content safety. This matters because a skill is only useful when the result is current, source-backed, and specific enough to use.

For users, the visible effect is simple: richer cards, better source attribution, more direct links, and fewer generic answers when a provider can return real data.

## 5. Better embeds and previews

Embeds became more useful throughout the app. Search results, booking links, generated files, code outputs, images and public examples got clearer previews and fullscreen views, so you can inspect results without losing the conversation context.

## 6. More useful examples and public pages

Announcements, tips, legal pages and example chats became proper public chat pages. That makes it easier to share what OpenMates can do and to open useful examples again later.

## 7. Smoother signup and payment options

OpenMates also added SEPA bank transfers via Revolut Business, improved Stripe checkout for users outside the EU, and added account email changes. These are not flashy features, but they make the basics less fragile when you actually want to use the product.

# What this means for everyday use

OpenMates should feel more like a useful workspace now: answers can contain learning links, you can mark and revisit important parts, more app skills can return real structured results, and public examples are easier to share.

As always, a lot of the work was also invisible bug fixing and reliability improvements — especially around encrypted chat sync, embeds, signup, and Safari behavior.

Greetings,

Marco  
Creator of OpenMates

title.text: v0.11: Code tools, daily inspirations & new media providers

description.text: Plus a short recap of the v0.10 improvements

message.text:
Hey there,

OpenMates v0.11 is now live. This update builds on the v0.10 improvements and adds practical everyday features: richer Daily Inspirations, code execution, repository research, music generation, image-generation provider improvements, clearer app results, and local interface fonts.

# First, a quick v0.10 recap

v0.10 added Wikipedia links inside answers, message highlights and comments, better public announcement/example pages, SEPA bank transfers, and account email changes.

Those changes made OpenMates more useful as a daily workspace: easier to learn from, easier to share, and less fragile around the account and payment basics.

# ✨ What is new in v0.11

## 1. Expanded Daily Inspirations

Daily Inspirations became richer and more varied. They can surface public videos, useful feature ideas, and concrete starting points for things you may want to do in OpenMates.

The goal is to make OpenMates feel less like an empty chatbot box and more like a place that helps you discover useful things to do: research a topic, understand a video, plan a task, explore a tool, or continue from an example.

## 2. Code execution and code research improvements

The Code app got a big step forward. OpenMates can now run code in a sandbox, show outputs, help with repository searches, and handle more code-related follow-up actions.

For everyday users this is useful even if you are not a professional developer: small scripts, data cleanup, document generation, website previews, log explanations, and technical questions can become more interactive.

## 3. Music generation and image provider improvements

v0.11 expands generated-media workflows with music generation and improvements around image-generation providers. That means OpenMates can support more creative tasks directly in chat: making a quick music idea, generating visual concepts, iterating on prompts, or turning a rough idea into media you can actually inspect and reuse.

The work also improves how generated media is presented, so results are easier to preview, open, and continue from.

## 4. Clearer app results and provider details

Many app cards and embed previews now show better real examples, provider logos, source information and clearer metadata. This makes it easier to understand what happened, where a result came from, and which app skill was used.

For daily use, that means less guessing: travel results, web results, generated files, media outputs, and code results should be easier to recognize and act on.

## 5. Better follow-up presentation

Follow-up suggestions already existed, but their presentation is now cleaner and easier to use. They are meant to help you continue a task without having to think of the perfect next prompt yourself.

## 6. Local interface fonts

You can now choose local interface font preferences. It is a small setting, but it matters if you spend a lot of time reading and writing in OpenMates.

## 7. Stability and performance improvements

There were also stability and performance improvements in chat sync, embeds, file previews, and image result previews.

# What comes next

The next step is to keep making OpenMates easier to understand and easier to use: better examples, clearer app flows, more polished creative and research tools, and fewer rough edges in the chat experience.

Thanks for using OpenMates and for giving feedback when something feels confusing or broken.

Greetings,

Marco  
Creator of OpenMates
